questions.stem: Sanjana, 30, is jaundiced after a trip to Thailand. As part of your focused GP examination you tell the examiner you will look for hepatic encephalopathy by checking for asterixis. How should you elicit this sign?
options: Arms outstretched, palms up, eyes closed; watch about 30 seconds for downward drift
Arms outstretched, palms down, paper on the fingers; watch for a fine tremor
Arms outstretched, wrists dorsiflexed, fingers spread; watch about 30 seconds for a flap
Repeated finger-to-nose testing with eyes open; watch for a tremor near the target
questions.why: Asterixis is a negative myoclonus. Sustained wrist extension briefly lapses, so the hands flap. Hold the arms out with wrists cocked back and fingers spread for about 15 to 30 seconds. In hepatitis A it is a sign of encephalopathy and means hospital.
notes: This tests for pronator drift, a sign of an upper motor neurone lesion, not of metabolic encephalopathy.
A sheet of paper shows a fine postural tremor, as in thyrotoxicosis or sympathomimetic use, not the coarse flap of asterixis.
Finger-to-nose testing shows a cerebellar intention tremor. It does not show the lapses in posture that produce asterixis.

questions.stem: Sanjana, 30, has acute hepatitis A and is being managed at home. Four days later she comes back to the GP for repeat bloods. She is fully oriented and managing small meals. Which new result would most warrant urgent referral to ED or hepatology?
options: INR 1.6, with albumin unchanged at 44 g/L
ALT risen to 1250 U/L, with INR 1.1
Bilirubin risen to 120 µmol/L, with INR 1.1
ALP risen to 260 U/L, with GGT 110 U/L
questions.why: INR and mental state are the markers of evolving acute liver failure. In acute hepatitis A, an INR of 1.5 or more needs urgent hospital or hepatology assessment. The size of the transaminase rise does not predict prognosis.
notes: Transaminase levels reflect active hepatocyte injury, not prognosis. With a normal INR and normal mental state she can still be managed at home with close review.
A rising bilirubin with preserved synthetic function and a clear mental state is common in the icteric phase. It calls for close follow-up, not urgent transfer.
A rising ALP and GGT reflects the cholestatic phase of hepatitis A. It does not mean liver failure while the INR stays normal.

questions.stem: Sanjana, 30, has acute hepatitis A with a bilirubin of 88 µmol/L, 66 of it conjugated. She reports dark urine and pale stools. What is the best explanation for these two symptoms?
options: Unconjugated bilirubin spills into urine, and less is turned into urobilinogen in the gut
Haemolysis raises urobilinogen, which darkens the urine while the stools stay pale
Bile salts build up and darken the urine, while their loss from the gut bleaches stool
Conjugated bilirubin is water-soluble so enters urine, and less reaches gut as stercobilin
questions.why: In hepatitis, conjugated bilirubin leaks back into the blood instead of draining into bile. It is water-soluble, so the kidneys filter it and the urine darkens. Less bilirubin reaches the gut to become stercobilin, so the stools go pale.
notes: Unconjugated bilirubin is bound to albumin and is not water-soluble, so it is not filtered into the urine (acholuric jaundice).
Haemolysis causes unconjugated jaundice with normal or dark stools. Her haemoglobin is normal and most of her bilirubin is conjugated.
Retained bile salts cause itch, but bile salts do not colour the urine. Stool colour comes from stercobilin, a bilirubin product.

questions.stem: Sanjana, 30, has fever, jaundice and right upper quadrant pain. Cholangitis and cholecystitis are on your differential. You tell the examiner you will test for Murphy's sign. Where do you place your fingers to press over the gallbladder fundus?
options: Right fifth intercostal space in the midclavicular line
Tip of the right ninth costal cartilage, at the lateral edge of rectus abdominis
Two-thirds of the way from the umbilicus to the right anterior superior iliac spine
Right renal angle, between the twelfth rib and the erector spinae
questions.why: The gallbladder fundus lies at the tip of the right ninth costal cartilage. This is where the lateral border of rectus abdominis (linea semilunaris) meets the costal margin, on the transpyloric plane. Press there while the patient breathes in.
notes: The fifth intercostal space in the midclavicular line is roughly the upper border of liver dullness on percussion. It is not the surface marking of the gallbladder.
This is McBurney's point, the surface marking of the appendix base, and is used when assessing for appendicitis.
The renal angle is where you test for kidney tenderness, as in pyelonephritis. It is posterior and well away from the gallbladder.
